Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a workout into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme workout and deliver a live timeline: Erg Session — four rowers, two machines for 4 rowers, 2 ergs, 3 pieces
Resource limits: two ergs, four rowers, one coach, one rower on the coached drill at a time.
No finishing time was given; finish as early as the work allows.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Erg Session — four rowers, two machines

Two ergs in the bay and four of us, so we row in pairs and the pair that is off the machines is the pair that is resting. A and B are the first pair, C and D the second. Nobody sits on a machine they are not rowing.

Warm-up
A and B warm up first: 10 minutes, rate 18, light pressure, half slide to full slide.
C and D come in ten minutes later and take the machines for their own 10 minute warm-up.

The pieces
Three pieces, four minutes each, rate 26 to 28, target split on the monitor.
A and B take the first piece as soon as C and D are off the machines.
C and D take the first piece straight off the back of A and B's first piece.
A and B start their second piece four minutes after their first one ends.
C and D take the second piece as soon as A and B are off.
A and B start their third piece four minutes after their second one ends.
C and D take the third piece as soon as A and B are off.

Technique drill
Three minutes each, one at a time, coach on the machine with you: pause at the finish, pause at half slide, then build. A goes first once C and D are off the last piece, then B, then C, then D.

Cooldown
Ten minutes on the floor together once the last drill is done: legs up the wall, hips, lats, then a cup of tea.

Coach
Brief the crew on the boards before anyone gets on: 5 minutes.
Call splits from the first piece: 20 minutes on the clock, watch the catch not the monitor.
Run the drills: 12 minutes, one rower at a time, straight through.
Debrief after the cooldown: 10 minutes, what the splits said and what Saturday looks like.

Note
The rests are not steps for the first pair: they are the gap between one piece ending and the next one starting, because the machines are handed over in that gap and the second pair is using them. The second pair's rests are the first pair's pieces. That is the whole design of the session.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

End your reply with the same read-back as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json
{
  "summary": "one paragraph: what is being made, for how many, by when, under what constraints",
  "servesOrScale": "8 people",
  "deadline": "2026-11-26T18:00:00",
  "constraints": ["one oven", "two burners", "two cooks"]
}
```

This is a Rhylthyme workout timeline for one coach and four rowers using only two erg machines. The crew splits into two pairs, A/B and C/D, so the session is fundamentally a machine handoff exercise: while one pair rows a four-minute piece, the other pair is off the machines in the gap before its next piece, and the three pieces per pair alternate this way. The coach has separate duties that must be held or started at specific moments: a five-minute briefing before anyone gets on, split-calling for twenty minutes from the first piece, twelve minutes of coached drills one rower at a time after the last piece, and a ten-minute debrief after the ten-minute floor cooldown. There is no requested deadline, so the program should finish as early as the mandatory sequence, the two-machine limit, the one-at-a-time drill limit, and the need for the four rowers to do the cooldown together allow. The source does not appear truncated; the exact target split on the monitor is unspecified, but it does not change the timing.

```json
{
  "summary": "A live-clocked erg session for four rowers using two machines, with one coach running prep, split-calling, drills, and debrief; A/B and C/D work as alternating pairs, so a pair’s rest between its own pieces is the other pair’s piece, drills happen one rower at a time with the coach, and the cooldown is all four together on the floor. No absolute finish time was given, so the goal is to start as soon as the coach briefs and finish as early as the mandatory sequence and shared-machine/coach limits allow. The source appears complete, except that the numeric target split is not specified.",
  "servesOrScale": "4 rowers, 2 erg machines, 1 coach",
  "deadline": "No deadline; finish as early as the work allows",
  "constraints": [
    "two ergs only; only two rowers can be on machines at once",
    "four rowers total, paired as A+B and C+D",
    "one coach available for brief, split calls, drills, and debrief",
    "only one rower can take a coached drill at a time",
    "rowers may not sit on machines they are not actively rowing",
    "a pair’s rest between its pieces is the other pair’s piece on the machines",
    "coach briefs for five minutes before anyone gets on",
    "coach calls splits for twenty minutes from the first piece",
    "coach runs twelve minutes of drills after the last piece",
    "ten-minute cooldown on the floor together after the last drill",
    "ten-minute debrief after the cooldown",
    "no wall-clock finish time was provided"
  ]
}
```

A Rhylthyme track is one sequential line of work; its steps cannot overlap, while anything that happens at the same time belongs in a separate track. A step has exactly one duration kind: `fixed` with `seconds`, `variable` with `minSeconds`, `maxSeconds`, and `defaultSeconds`, or `indefinite` until the person ends it. A startTrigger anchors that step to `programStart`, `programStartOffset`, another step via `afterStep`, a buffered after-step trigger, a manual tap, an abort, or a compound condition. `stepId`s are unique across the whole program, not just within one track. Every `task` occupied by a step needs a matching `resourceConstraints` entry, and that entry’s `maxConcurrent` is the shared-resource limiter, such as one oven, one coach, or two ergs. Repeated work should use `replicates` on one step rather than copied steps or tracks, chaining per-instance work with `instances: "each"`, barrier steps with `instances: "all"`, and using `maxInFlight` when a holding area only fits `k` instances at once.

Resource constraints I expect for this workout:

- `erg` — `maxConcurrent: 2` — two rowing machines; four rowers use them in pairs, but only two rower-machine steps can overlap at once.
- `coach` — `maxConcurrent: 1` — one coach; one coach handles briefing, split calling, drills, and debrief.
- `coached_drill` — `maxConcurrent: 1` — one rower at a time on the coached drill; this is the explicit drill slot, with one rower plus the coach working at that moment.
- `floor` — `maxConcurrent: 5` — cooldown floor work; four rowers are together on the floor, and the coach may also be present, so five people are the maximum occupied there.
- `actors` — five people total: four rowers and one coach. Rests between pieces should not be declared as machine-rest resources; they are timing gaps created by handoffs.

```json
{
  "acknowledgement": "tracks are sequential lines of work; one duration kind per step; triggers link steps or the clock; stepIds are global; every task needs a resourceConstraint; repeated work uses replicates with instances each/all and maxInFlight only for holding-area limits",
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "erg", "maxConcurrent": 2 },
    { "task": "coach", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "coached_drill", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "floor", "maxConcurrent": 5 }
  ],
  "actors": 5
}
```

Turn 3 of 4 — extraction. Steps only: no tracks, no triggers, no program JSON.

Imagine you have to carry out this workout yourself, in a gym where you have: two ergs, four rowers, one coach, one rower on the coached drill at a time, and everything must be ready at the earliest time the work allows. You have only the text below. Read all of it.

List every timed activity you would have to perform, in the order the text gives it, with:

- a short kebab-case `stepId` and a human `name`;
- `task`: the resource it occupies while it runs — the oven, a burner, the thermocycler, the PA, the bench, your own hands. Use the same name every time for the same resource;
- how long it takes: exact (`fixed`), a range (`variable`), or "until I decide" (`indefinite`);
- `sourceSpan`: the exact words in the text you took it from, as `{"quote": "...", "occurrence": n}`, where n says which occurrence of those words you mean (1 for the first). Quote the text verbatim — do not paraphrase it;
- `inferred`: `true` for a step the text never states but the work needs anyway (preheating, thawing, resting, cooling, labelling, sound-check), with `"sourceSpan": null`. Keep these few and obvious.

Split anything the text bundles into one sentence when the parts occupy different resources or different stretches of time ("brown the meat, then simmer for 40 minutes" is two activities). Do not decide yet which activities can overlap, which track they belong to, or what waits for what.

Reply with the step list as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json
{
  "steps": [
    {
      "stepId": "roast-turkey",
      "name": "Roast the turkey",
      "task": "oven",
      "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 10800 },
      "sourceSpan": { "quote": "Roast the turkey for 3 hours", "occurrence": 1 },
      "inferred": false
    },
    {
      "stepId": "rest-turkey",
      "name": "Rest the turkey",
      "task": "counter",
      "duration": { "type": "variable", "minSeconds": 1200, "maxSeconds": 2400, "defaultSeconds": 1800 },
      "sourceSpan": { "quote": "let it rest", "occurrence": 1 },
      "inferred": false
    },
    {
      "stepId": "preheat-oven",
      "name": "Preheat the oven",
      "task": "oven",
      "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 900 },
      "sourceSpan": null,
      "inferred": true
    }
  ]
}
```

Turn 4 of 4 — relationships, then the program.

Take the step list from turn 3 exactly as it stands.

**First, tracks.** Put each step in a track: one track per parallel line of work — per dish, per station, per instrument, per performer, per sample group. Steps in one track run one after another and must not overlap; anything that runs while something else runs belongs in its own track.

**Second, triggers.** Give every step a `startTrigger` from this vocabulary and no other:

- `{"type":"programStart"}` — at t = 0.
- `{"type":"programStartOffset","offsetSeconds":n}` — n seconds after the start; this is how a short track is delayed so it finishes with the others.
- `{"type":"afterStep","stepId":"x"}` — when x ends. Add `"offsetSeconds"` for a gap, `"event":"start"` to hang off x's start instead of its end, `"instances"` when x is replicated.
- `{"type":"afterStepWithBuffer","stepId":"x","bufferSeconds":n}` — n seconds after x ends.
- `{"type":"manual"}` — the person taps to start it: a gate that no clock can predict (guests seated, dough looks right, the surgeon is ready).
- `{"type":"compound","logic":"all"|"any","triggers":[...]}` — wait for all of, or the first of, several triggers.

**Third, refine the question before you answer it.** Within the scope of scheduling these activities for one person to follow, suggest a better version of the question "which activities depend on which, and which can run at the same time?" — one that would expose dependencies this text implies but does not state: things that must cool, rest, preheat, thaw, proof, be held warm, or be ready at the same moment as something else. Write your improved question out, answer it, and revise the triggers accordingly. A step the improved question reveals is added here, marked `"inferred": true`.

**Then emit the complete program JSON** in a single ```json fenced block: `schemaVersion`, `programId`, `name`, `environmentType`, `actors`, `tracks`, and a `resourceConstraints` entry for every `task` any step uses. Carry turn 3's provenance onto each step as `"metadata": {"sourceSpan": ..., "inferred": ...}`.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "0.3.0-alpha",
  "programId": "kebab-case-id",
  "name": "Human title",
  "environmentType": "kitchen",
  "actors": 2,
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "turkey",
      "name": "Turkey",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "preheat-oven",
          "name": "Preheat the oven",
          "task": "oven",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 900 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "metadata": { "sourceSpan": null, "inferred": true }
        },
        {
          "stepId": "roast-turkey",
          "name": "Roast the turkey",
          "task": "oven",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 10800 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "afterStep", "stepId": "preheat-oven" },
          "metadata": { "sourceSpan": { "quote": "Roast the turkey for 3 hours", "occurrence": 1 }, "inferred": false }
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "oven", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "counter", "maxConcurrent": 2 }
  ],
  "metadata": { "serves": "8" }
}
```

Then finish the job with the tools:
1. If the public catalog already covers this (search_public_recipes or start_workout), load that instead and stop — its result already has the live URL.
2. Otherwise keep the program you just built; `rhylthyme://guide/authoring` is the cheat-sheet and `rhylthyme://examples/*` are complete programs to pattern-match.
3. Express the limits as constraints, not as copied JSON: the `resourceConstraints`, `replicates`, `instances` and `maxInFlight` you confirmed in turn 2.
4. Run validate_program and fix every error it reports.
5. Run analyze_schedule to check the makespan, critical path and resource conflicts; adjust offsets so tracks finish together. Its `bindingConstraints` say which limit is actually gating the makespan.
6. Call visualize_schedule and give the user the live URL plus the Gantt/itinerary from the result. Do not describe the schedule in prose.
